slides.title: Sleeping Machines
slides.subtitle: The next general-purpose substrate for machine intelligence.
slides.notes: Sleeping Machines aims to be the next general-purpose substrate for machine intelligence: one trainable architecture, learning rule and execution model spanning language and reasoning, multimodal world models, embodiment, event-native analytics, continual learning, communication, self-design and datacenter, edge and clockless hardware. Private review deck. The founder proposes a €3M raise. €50M priced pre-money is the central bullish negotiating thesis developed here; €100M is a stretch scenario, neither an independent fair-value appraisal nor an investor offer. The research evidence is exploratory and single-seed. No customer interest has been reported. No investor, vendor or customer has been contacted in preparing this deck.

slides.title: One substrate for learning, representing and executing intelligence.
slides.subtitle: Different forms of experience can teach reusable computations within the same learner.

body.label: MANY FORMS OF EXPERIENCE
body.body: Tokens, sensors, typed tables and process traces. Synchronous samples and asynchronous events.

shared.label: ONE TRAINABLE SUBSTRATE
shared.body: Addressed messages, persistent memory and temporal races. End-to-end credit learns content, timing and unrealized alternatives.

mind.label: REUSABLE INTELLIGENCE
mind.body: Transfer between perception, reasoning and action. Continual learning and self-design.

slides.transfer: The platform thesis: knowledge learned from one form of experience can become useful computation in another.
slides.opportunity: Time and sleeps perform computation. Target: clockless learning and inference, capacity beyond activity, small data to large scale.
slides.banner: First bridge: mixed-type tables through the temporal core. First transfer proof: joint learning, retained skills, matched work.
slides.notes: AGI here means the long-term ambition of broadly transferable learning and competence across domains, not a claim that a shared graph or computational universality guarantees intelligence. The visual is a proposed family composition, not an implemented robotics system. Common content/time/address/state interfaces can connect asynchronous sensory and motor events with language and deliberation; local dense regions, joins and batching remain available. No global periodic tick is required by the family, but causal ordering, timers and task/actuator deadlines remain. Fast persistent state and slower learned rules offer a path to online adaptation and memory-policy learning; fully native sparse asynchronous learning is still a research target. The opportunity is to test whether embodied experience teaches transferable causal, geometric and planning abstractions and whether cognitive learning improves action, using shared representations and credit. Both directions require separate held-out, matched-data/work comparisons with joint dense/VLA, isolated-module and stopped-credit controls, including retention, replay and system resources. Existing PaLM-E and RT-2 demonstrate related joint-learning or web-to-control precedents; we do not claim that conventional models cannot integrate these domains. Neither precedent establishes our proposed motor-to-cognitive transfer or our cost advantage. Shared parameters do not establish AGI, and no project embodied-transfer/robot-control experiment has completed. Platform upside is conditional and correlated with the same unresolved learning and execution risks; it is not an extra independent valuation or an assigned probability. See INVESTOR_PROOF_PLAN.md for staged work and the smallest simulated transfer protocol; no queue or new compute is reserved by this slide. Editorial update 5 October: the platform thesis encompasses heterogeneous representations, shared learning and execution semantics, and small-to-large operating regimes. Mixed-type tabular success would be evidence of this unification; numeric-only tabular fits are not that proof. Joint skill transfer, clockless learning hardware and scaling advantages require their own completed comparisons.

slides.title: Intelligence must compose across experience and execution.
slides.subtitle: A common substrate connects what a model learns with how and where it computes.
slides.notes: This is the problem definition and investment hypothesis. It is not a claim that all existing architectures perform dense work or lack memory. MoE already separates available parameters from selected computation; recurrent and selective-state models already retain state. Our proposed contribution is a temporal race/state/alternative-credit construction and its tested consequences. Software and hardware benefits must be evaluated with tuned incumbents under the same workload boundaries.

slides.core:
One interface for content, timing, memory address and state, from single units to complete systems.
Target: computation through timing, sparse memory updates, small messages, and learning from unchosen paths.
slides.caveat: Mamba and attention containments are exact identities with numerical checks; other relationships are design relationships to be measured.
slides.notes: This is the whole-family position, not a claim that every implemented member contains every incumbent. The envelope intersects recurrent/SSM, attention, sparse expert, statistical/retrieval, adaptive-memory and temporal systems. Supported dense reference blocks and synchronous barriers are permitted endpoints. The proposed differentiation is a common stateful temporal/selection/credit construction and its eventual quality/resource behavior. Known primitives have prior art; wrapping a reference predictor establishes no advantage. Computational universality is not a strictly larger class than all finite computable predictors. The technical report states operator, state, precision and schedule conditions. Current language fits illustrate one branch; joint TTT, multimodal integration, general morphing and clockless hardware economics are separate milestones. Containment (7 Oct 2026): a Mamba selective scan is the family member in which each token arrives after a learned content-dependent delay, memories decay over elapsed time, and writes/reads are content-addressed; experiments/theory/mamba_containment_check.py reproduces Mamba-1 and Mamba-2 selective scans to 4e-13 (float64); rotating memories extend the class. Attention: an exponential race samples exactly from a softmax and delay-coded aggregation reproduces softmax attention over delivered keys (THEORY notes 08, 151). Neither identity claims speed or learning-efficiency parity at scale.

slides.title: Choose the right computation in each region.
slides.subtitle: One family can mix selective temporal programs with rich interaction and causal memory.

steps.label: 01 / UNITS
steps.body: Each unit chooses what to remember, what message to send and when. Timing itself performs computation.

steps.label: 02 / LAYERS
steps.body: A layer can activate one message or many: dense where needed, lean elsewhere.

steps.label: 03 / COMPOSITIONS
steps.body: Learned features, counts and stored history can all inform the same prediction.

steps.label: 04 / SYSTEMS
steps.body: The same learning rule works in batches or on a live stream, including learning after deployment.

slides.banner: No global clock is required. Combined models, learning-after-deployment gains and chip energy are still milestones.
slides.notes: The local choices form a generative design space, not a catalogue of unrelated benchmark models. Selective and full-support regions can coexist; synchronous barriers are optional local schedules inside event semantics. The same model structure supports causal parameter updates and batching. Current state/statistical adaptation and an online pilot are scoped evidence; they do not establish fully asynchronous on-chip learning or a general TTT gain. Learned event routes already adapt execution inside a fixed graph; operator selection, reception/depth choice, allocation and growth/pruning require future utility, state/version migration and resource accounting. The formal core defines twelve fields and compatibility rules, and illustrative complete members show contrasting constructions without adding benchmark evidence. Preserve computation, representation and trainability through interfaces; forward equality, learning preservation and lower cost are distinct contracts. Learned memory/scheduling can be viewed as fast-state adaptation governed by slow trained rules, drawing on memory-augmented meta-learning and TTT. The opportunity register defines native irregular ingestion, asynchronous codecs and joint embodied/cognitive paths with explicit first proofs. The prior-art boundary and full work/bit accounting are stated in the report.

slides.title: Messages race. Selected memories update. Alternatives learn.
slides.subtitle: A simple event loop connects representation, timing and sparse computation.
slides.notes: This construction combines familiar vector operations with temporal computation and sparse state. Separate keys determine addressing; values determine delivered content. Counterfactual credit gives unrealized alternatives a learning signal without softening the hard forward route. The present implementation is not a physical asynchronous machine: autograd, shared training windows, clipping and Adam remain. Winner-only inference still scores all candidate keys.

steps.label: 01 / ENCODE
steps.body: A learned function produces a message and its arrival time from input and local memory.

steps.label: 02 / SELECT
steps.body: Arrival times select a receiver. Separate address keys and delivered values support sparse execution.

steps.label: 03 / REMEMBER
steps.body: Update the selected memory and propagate a new message into deeper computation.

steps.label: 04 / LEARN
steps.body: Use errors to improve message content and timing, including paths that were not selected.

slides.banner: Implemented and trained today in ordinary software (CPU); no special hardware needed to run it.

Its parent family, deep state-space models, is general on dense sequences and language; published SSM results do not, to our knowledge, show one model winning event likelihood and sparse clinical classification together. Track G (experiments/GENERALITY_PLAN.md): self-supervised event pretraining on unlabeled clinical records transferred to mortality prediction with fewer labels (G1); one model across five event datasets (G2); PAM wearable sensors (G3); event-to-event transfer (G4). Update 8 Oct 07:40: PAM (wearable activity recognition) five-split TEST protocol, pre-registered 7 Oct 19:42 UTC: accuracy 0.9775 ± 0.0074, F1 0.9803 ± 0.0080 vs MTM 0.975 ± 0.002 / 0.976 ± 0.002, 46,316 parameters; per split 0.979, 0.981, 0.981, 0.981, 0.964 (split 4 behind). Win under the pre-registered rule (mean accuracy ahead).

slides.title: Respect types. Race decisions. Compose learned state.
slides.subtitle: Meaningful comparisons become events before evidence enters a common neural representation.
slides.notes: Theory and39stdlibcontracts in experiments/theory/TYPED_SEMANTICS_AND_RACE_COMPOSITION_20261006.md and experiments/results/diagnostics/typed_semantics_composition_contracts_20261006_v1.json. A raw affine gate cannot use arbitrary nominal codes and remain invariant to every code permutation with fixed parameters. Categorical embeddings and feature-specific neural maps are legal alternatives. Under invariant typed event adapters, identical causal core/state/RNG produce identical outputs. Learning additionally requires appropriate preprocessing, initialization and optimizer coordinates. Joint comparison credit must retain computational time and factual derivatives. FT-Transformer and NODE already provide typed/neural-tree precedents. Our construction integrates the interface with temporal races, persistent addressed state and actual alternative credit. Current synthetic witness uses fixed predicates; no learned-threshold or real-tree benchmark advantage is claimed.

cards.label: RESPECT THE FIELD
cards.body: Compare a quantity with a threshold in its units. Test category membership, Boolean conditions and missingness explicitly. Category codes need no invented distance or order.

cards.label: LEARN THE DECISION
cards.body: Comparison outcomes feed computational races and selected memory writes. Counterfactual consequences teach routes. Learned thresholds require branch, timing and factual-path credit; that extension is the next test.

cards.label: COMPOSE THE EVIDENCE
cards.body: After a typed interface, learned vectors can mix meaningfully in persistent representations. The same event construction can connect tables, tokens, process traces and actions.

slides.banner: Typed semantics + conditional selection + deep temporal learning. First mixed-type fit:100% synthetic DEV accuracy; fixed predicates.

This gives {transformer_fit_ratio:.2f}× lower fitting arithmetic and {transformer_parameter_ratio:.2f}× fewer parameters for this saved control, with {transformer_credit_gain:.4f} lower bpc. The strong one-pass LSTM is {lstm_bpc:.6f} at 20.306 TFLOPs. Best native p96 is {best_bpc:.6f} at 58.648 TFLOPs. Low-batch inference is a proposed test venue for stateful sparse execution, not a measured region of advantage. No customer interest has been reported; demand interviews and evaluation partners remain future work.

slides.title: Software proves the advantage. Hardware multiplies it.
slides.subtitle: One research program, with staged routes to deployment.
slides.notes: Hardware is a multiplier on the software result, applied to different parts of the energy budget. Largest lever: memory locality and sparse activity (DRAM read ~640 pJ vs ~3.7 pJ float multiply at 45 nm, Horowitz 2014); dense low-batch inference streams all weights per token, our model reads a few local state slots per event. Clock removal adds: no clock-tree power, average-case latency, near-threshold voltage tolerance, leakage-only idle capacity, and thermal headroom for memory-on-logic stacking and modular chiplets. Training locally is plausible (route credit and delay/gate updates are local) but the current trainer uses non-local backprop and clipping; a local learning rule is a milestone. Event-driven, memory-local chips exist (Loihi 2 and others); the field lacks a competitive trainable model, which is our licensing opening. No Sleeping Machines chip or joule measurement exists; baselines for hardware claims are competent clock-gated, SRAM-heavy synchronous designs as well as GPUs. Details: HARDWARE_THESIS.md.

cards.label: 01 / MODELS + RUNTIME
cards.body: Validate the language workload on existing hardware. License a model/runtime with auditable deployment economics.

cards.label: 02 / MEMORY-LOCAL ACCELERATORS
cards.body: Modeled per character: 1.7× fewer memory bytes than the best tuned Transformer and 5.8× fewer than the saved one, both beaten. 10× more memory adds 5% traffic. Tuned LSTMs: parity.

cards.label: 03 / CLOCKLESS SILICON
cards.body: No global clock: idle parts draw almost no power, answers arrive as soon as they are ready, and cool chips allow dense 3D stacking. Also the missing model for neuromorphic chips.

slides.title: The same model improves when unchosen paths receive credit.
slides.subtitle: Controlled small-model comparison; held-out error and estimated complete training work.
slides.notes: The local linearized credit estimator adds a derivative pathway for alternative delivered values while preserving the forward winner. It is not the exact full counterfactual trajectory gradient. The paired p32 / D4 T256 gain is {credit_gain:.6f} bpc, with {credit_fit_increase_pct:.4f}% extra whole-fit estimated operations. The corresponding p32 / D8 gain is {depth_credit_gain:.6f}. Attribution is stronger than a comparison between different widths, but a single seed still leaves variance and hyperparameter sensitivity unresolved.
stats: Timing-only credit versus added local alternative-value route credit.
Hard forward selection and parameter count retained.
Derived from the BPC difference; one controlled seed.
slides.detail: A deeper variant also improves by {depth_credit_gain:.3f} bits per character. Both are single-seed comparisons; numerical details and model definitions follow.
slides.banner: A falsifiable architectural mechanism, with a small counted arithmetic increment.

slides.title: More available state. The same eight selected writes.
slides.subtitle: Small model with alternative credit: available memory doubles; selected updates stay fixed.
slides.notes: Pool 2 → 4 changes memory scalars from 512 to 1,024 and parameters from 108,875 to 177,019. At T256, quality changes from {credit_bpc:.6f} to {pool_bpc:.6f}. Selected writes remain eight per input position; candidate keys increase 16 → 32. Winner-only per-position arithmetic increases {pool_sparse_increase_pct:.4f}%, but whole-fit estimated work rises {pool_fit_increase_pct:.4f}%. All memory and key scoring still cost resources. A negative uncredited pool expansion was measured at D8, while this positive credited pair is D4; this is not a full matched 2×2 interaction test.
slides.banner: Quality improves by {pool_gain:.3f} bpc; total capacity and learning costs remain explicitly charged.

slides.title: The sparse path is implemented; system proof is next.
slides.subtitle: Inference arithmetic per predicted character. Green bars: our implemented sparse runtime, which computes only the selected paths.
slides.notes: Small random float64 fixtures match full-emulator logits within roughly 1e-10. Actual trained float32 winner/state/cache parity and a full held-out rescore are prepared and pending. The prepared CPU worker retains prepacked matrices per fixed model version, but native admission remains unrun. Candidate key scans, copying, residency, setup, gather traffic, cache invalidation and quality must all be included in serving comparisons. The deck deliberately does not attach the trained quality to an unverified production backend or convert FLOPs to joules.
slides.caveat: Arithmetic estimates, not measured service cost. Our evaluation also pays about two extra positions of warm-up per predicted character; the LSTM evaluates differently.

slides.title: An adaptation signal exists. Its work is accounted for.
slides.subtitle: Predict-before-update experiment on a new text stream; separate from the latest model family.
slides.notes: Frozen versus online evaluation scores 8,191 targets with predict-before-update, 16-character delayed-feedback blocks, lr 1e-4, fresh Adam, clipping and full-backbone gradients. Both arms retain persistent local state. BPC improves by {online_gain:.6f}; total processing-operation estimates increase from 210,902,697 to 2,264,163,359, a {online_work_ratio:.4f}× ratio. This supports trainability under adaptation, not inexpensive lifelong learning. Retention, drift, long-horizon memory and local asynchronous learning need new evidence. Loihi 2 already provides an on-chip learning precedent.
slides.banner: Online-learning upside: persistent adaptive systems. Current result: one costed pilot.

slides.title: One substrate can support new communication and learning patterns.
slides.subtitle: Application hypotheses with first proofs; no codec, embodied-transfer or AGI result yet. The first row needs no special hardware.
rows: Built-in biases: computational time, first-arrival races, separate state per concurrent process.
FAS v1 is solved by a simple route rule (AUROC 0.755 at 256 events vs our 0.600); proof needs a harder v2 with ambiguous interleaving.
Addressed events retain time and update persistent programs. Dense regions remain available.
Same causal data/queries; compare timestamp-aware controls and burst/idle resource use.
Learn what, where and when to send; decoder retains predictive state.
Actual bytes versus distortion/task quality, sender/receiver work and causal latency.
Slow rules learn fast writes, retention, retrieval and scheduling from later utility.
Held-out delayed-use tasks; complete useful-return credit against immediate utility.
Shared sensing/action/language paths can exchange learned physical abstractions.
Motor-to-cognitive and reverse transfer measured separately; matched data/work and isolated-path controls.
slides.notes: The register in report/model_family_opportunities.md records six opportunities, mechanisms, evidence status, primary precedents and proof conditions. Dense arithmetic does not inherently require regularized input; variable-rate codecs and joint VLA models already exist. Our opportunity is coherent temporal/selective integration. Quantized message streams need a real wire/decoder contract; metadata/timing/reset and all endpoint work count. Joint motor/cognitive training needs shared information/credit and measured transfer; it does not prove AGI. Proposed application breadth supports platform optionality, not summed TAM or independent success chances. Existing integrated research queues retain priority.

slides.title: The contribution is the complete construction.
slides.subtitle: Established alternatives already address parts of this problem; they remain essential controls.
slides.notes: The pitch does not assert sole invention of sparse activation, gating, normalization, key/value separation or hardware learning. The latest native language model has no dense carrier or n-gram count component, but remains a restricted software realization. A weak result in one restricted variant should be diagnosed; genuine superiority requires matched strong controls. Intel Loihi 2 is cited on the adaptation and strategic slides.

Match quality/data and charge routing, memory traffic and training.
Persistent state and efficient sequence processing.
Test whether temporal races add useful quality or allocation.
Event-driven hardware and local learning precedents.
Prove expressive model quality, mapping and measured energy.
Joint timing, sparse memory, deep representation and alternative credit.
Scale integrated mechanisms without replacing them with dense carriers.

slides.title: What clockless, memory-local silicon can buy.
slides.subtitle: Physical mechanisms, their basis and what must be measured. No chip exists yet.

Dense models can also use SRAM-heavy or near-memory chips, and MoE partially decouples capacity from activity; our edge is the model's sparse, local access pattern, which must hold at competitive quality (P0-6 tuned baselines). rows: Cost model: 1.7–5.8× fewer bytes/char than the Transformers we beat; tuned LSTMs at parity; no clock tree.
Quality at large pools; chip-level measurement.
Average-case completion; events propagate when ready; races resolve at first arrival.
Event-trace latency on FPGA semantics prototype.
Low average power relieves the power-density limit: memory-on-logic 3D stacking, chiplets without a global timing domain.
Activity and peak-burst profiles on real streams.
Small messages sent only when events occur, not full vectors every clock: wire energy and wiring area track event rate.
Measured message rates and header overhead.
Addressed persistent state maps to banks beside compute; non-volatile memory makes dormant capacity near-free.
Locality and reuse-distance profile of trained models.
Route credit and delay/gate updates are local quantities.
Event-local learning rule matching current trainer quality.
Near-threshold voltage, native event sensors, low EMI, defect tolerance.

slides.title: Reverse-underwriting shows the assumptions behind a price.
slides.subtitle: This arithmetic is a sensitivity tool; the research does not estimate platform-success probabilities.
slides.notes: The illustrative model discounts the retained fraction of a successful future equity outcome to today and assigns zero failure value. It is not a complete corporate DCF, does not model all cash flows, and assumes the retained cohort benefits from an exit equity value after future financing. €10B exit × 30% retention / 1.15^10 is the conditional present value; €50M requires {required_probability_50_pct:.4f}% and €100M requires {required_probability_100_pct:.4f}%. These are neither forecasts nor inferred from small benchmarks. A €3M priced round at €50M pre-money gives {new_investor_pct:.4f}% initial investor ownership before option-pool changes, fees, preferences or future rounds; at €100M it gives {stretch_new_investor_pct:.4f}%. An investor must independently accept technology scalability, commercial value capture, rights and execution to support a premium price.
slides.banner: Required odds are reverse-calculated conditions. The benchmarks do not estimate those probabilities.

slides.title: The price depends on dilution, exit scale and time.
slides.subtitle: Required platform-success odds at 10 years and 15% discount; zero failure value.
slides.notes: This table is generated from the frozen financial model, not entered by hand. At a €3B outcome and 10% retained equity, the required probabilities are much higher than at a €30B exit with 50% retention. A lower discount rate increases the present value, while delays and dilution reduce it. In the €3M/€50M round, an investor retains 1.6981% at exit if 30% of its initial stake survives, giving €{conditional_proceeds_m_eur:.2f}M or {conditional_moic:.2f}× gross MOIC in the assumed €10B success outcome. That conditional upside is not expected return; failure is zero and cash-flow timing/preferences are omitted.
slides.caveat: Sensitivity assumptions only. Probabilities above 100% are infeasible in this model. Preferences, option pools and intermediate financing cash flows are omitted.

cards.label: IT LEARNS REAL TEXT
cards.body: Better than the 4-layer Transformer baseline (1.908) with 40% of its training compute. The larger LSTM (1.799) is still ahead.

cards.label: TRAINING UNCHOSEN PATHS HELPS
cards.body: Giving learning signal to the paths the model did not take cuts the error of the same small model, for 0.3% more training compute.

cards.label: MORE MEMORY, SAME RUNNING WORK
cards.body: Doubling memory slots lowers the error while each input still updates only 8 slots. Training cost rises; running cost barely changes.

slides.banner: Single runs on one dataset. The next proof is repeated runs plus a measured cost advantage.
